question: For fixed kernel models whose similarities depend only on which discrete input components match, what computations are possible on unseen component combinations, how do representational geometry and training-set coverage select among them, and which conclusions survive in feature-learning deep networks?

key_findings.claim: The central theorem gives a clean exact characterization of test behavior in the stated fixed-kernel regime: predictions are sums of functions of component conjunctions whose values occurred in at least one training example.
key_findings.evidence: A compositionally structured kernel depends only on the overlap set between two categorical inputs. Mobius inversion decomposes every such similarity into overlap-specific terms; because a zero-initialized/minimum-norm kernel predictor lies in the span of training representations, an unseen conjunction contributes no learned term. With two components, a held-out pair therefore receives only an intercept and two component-wise terms even though full-pair terms can fit arbitrary observed pairs. The result is exact for the representer-form predictor and specified training support, not a claim that every target function is intrinsically additive.

anchors.section: 4.3 Consequences for the compositional task space

key_findings.claim: The paper's definition of compositional structure is a strong exchangeability condition, not a synonym for generic modularity, factorization, disentanglement, or object-centricity.
key_findings.evidence: In the main definition, every pair of inputs sharing the same number of categorical components must have exactly the same inner product; the appendix relaxes this only so similarity may depend on the identity of the matched component positions. Similarity may not depend on which values matched, continuous distance within a factor, nuisance variation, or task-relevant relations among values. This symmetry deliberately removes non-compositional bases for generalization, but it excludes most learned representations and many realistic compositional problems.

key_findings.claim: Representational salience is a useful Mobius-transformed summary for the kernels studied, but its interpretation as a normalized positive subpopulation contribution is not valid for every compositionally structured positive-semidefinite kernel covered by the definition.
key_findings.evidence: The metric recursively subtracts lower-order overlap similarities and divides by the total nonempty increment. The manuscript supplies neither a positivity assumption nor a proof that every increment is nonnegative. A valid overlap kernel can have negative first-order Mobius coefficients, and a constant representation makes the normalizing denominator zero. Thus saliences can be negative or undefined outside the paper's plotted neural kernels; summing to one alone does not make them mixture proportions or literal neural subpopulations.

key_findings.claim: For a centered family of symbolic-addition splits, the paper derives an exact and interpretable memorization-leak formula.
key_findings.evidence: If the training set contains every pair with at least one component in a centered subset W of size p, the held-out prediction is m(v1+v2), where m=p*S(1;2)/(1+(p-2)S(1;2)). Any full-conjunction salience makes minimum-norm fitting spend capacity on observed pairs, compressing held-out sums; increasing component salience or p reduces the leak. The result depends on the centered value sets, the particular row/column support, unregularized minimum-norm/kernel fitting, scalar addition, and the salience being in the intended range.

key_findings.claim: The context-dependence experiments isolate a concrete shortcut competition between the correct context-feature conjunctions, a context-only predictor, and full-input memorization.
key_findings.evidence: Context dependence is expressible using the two context-feature pair terms that occur in training, so conjunction-wise additivity does not itself prevent success. On the most biased CD-3 split, context alone predicts two thirds of training labels; minimum-norm models with strong single-component and full-conjunction salience can use that shortcut and memorize exceptions, producing below-chance held-out accuracy. CD-1 and CD-2 weaken the correlation and are easier. This is a controlled synthetic demonstration, not a general theorem that the same salience comparison detects shortcuts in arbitrary datasets.

key_findings.claim: Transitive equivalence is a valuable negative-control task because unseen pair labels cannot be represented by the component-wise sum forced on a two-component held-out split.
key_findings.evidence: A fixed compositionally structured kernel can fit observed equality pairs using pair-conjunction features but those features are absent for a genuinely unseen pair. Unlike transitive ordering, equivalence cannot be recovered from a difference of scalar item ranks under this encoding and support. The impossibility is therefore specific to this fixed representation, readout, target encoding, and train/test construction; a representation already encoding class relations or a feature-learning model can escape it.

anchors.section: E.6 Transitive ordering and Appendix F

key_findings.claim: The deep-vision results support several qualitative trends, but they are small controlled studies rather than an exact validation of the kernel equations.
key_findings.evidence: Across ten jointly reseeded category assignments/model runs per condition, MNIST ConvNets and CIFAR-10 ResNets/ViTs show approximately linear held-out addition predictions, slopes that generally improve with spatial separation and training-set coverage, and the predicted CD-3 shortcut pattern. Error bars are standard errors over n=10, the ResNet/ViT fits are noisier, the ViT distance effect is subtle, some models do not fit training perfectly, and one p=4 interpolation/extrapolation comparison contradicts the invariant-slope prediction. No hypothesis tests, effect-size intervals, new datasets, language models, or scale sweep are reported.

key_findings.claim: The abstract and discussion overstate the strength of deep-network validation relative to the paper's own decisive appendix diagnostic.
key_findings.evidence: The abstract says the theory is empirically validated and captures ConvNets, ResNets, and ViTs. Appendix Figure 13 shows that the ConvNet NTK salience changes substantially during training, so the networks are not in the kernel regime; the authors state that the theory does not apply exactly, supplies no quantitative bounds, and misses the quantitative salience-slope relationship. The defensible conclusion is qualitative analogy on selected tasks, not validation of the fixed-kernel theorem for feature-learning deep networks.

anchors.section: E.1.3 NTK change during training and Figure 13

key_findings.claim: The final-version DSprites analysis is appropriately cautionary and directly falsifies the broad quantitative use of salience on realistic learned representations.
key_findings.evidence: The six VAE families aggregate 1,800 pretrained models and 50 task-role samples, but their overlap-structured approximation leaves a variance ratio of roughly 0.5 to 0.9. Average behavior is often highly conjunction-additive and transitive equivalence remains poor, yet addition error shows no predicted trend with S(1;2), shape is barely represented, and context performance is near chance. The paper explicitly concludes that its geometry analysis does not apply to these representations; averaging over task permutations also hides potentially systematic instance-level deviations.

key_findings.claim: The extension beyond exact compositional structure proves only an ensemble expectation under a deliberately independent, zero-mean Gaussian construction.
key_findings.evidence: For a representation formed by summing independent Gaussian vectors for every conjunction value, components unique to a test input have zero conditional expected inner product with the trained predictor. This makes the ensemble-average prediction conjunction-wise additive, while individual sampled models can be severely non-additive. Correlated residuals, structured similarities among factor values, learned entanglement, finite-task selection, or a single deployed representation are outside the result; the paper itself says it has no geometry guarantee for this scenario.

key_findings.claim: Feature learning is not a peripheral exception: it changes the computational class and supplies the paper's own counterexample to treating conjunction-wise limits as fundamental neural-network limits.
key_findings.evidence: Small-initialization one-hidden-layer ReLU networks learn shared sparse units for overlapping equality pairs and generalize on transitive equivalence, while lazy/kernel-regime networks fail. MNIST ConvNets also improve with component separation. The proposed sparse-unit mechanism is supported by weight plots but not a complete optimization theorem, and the paper notes that other feature-learning mechanisms may exist. These results make clear that the core impossibility applies to fixed representations/readouts, not neural networks without qualification.

anchors.section: F Shared-unit account and ConvNet result

key_findings.claim: Proposition B.2 may reflect a real deep-ReLU kernel phenomenon, but the proof printed in the reviewed version does not establish the stated result.
key_findings.evidence: The derivation says normalized correlations tend to infinity although they should approach one, contains inconsistent normalized/un-normalized denominators, and reduces contraction to 0<s<=1/2 even though overlaps with more than half the components give larger s. Its final strict inequality is asserted by visual inspection of a plot rather than proved. The cited earlier lemma may support a corrected theorem, but the self-contained proof as printed is incomplete, so the claim that very deep ReLU kernels exclusively encode the full conjunction should not be treated as certified from this manuscript alone.

anchors.section: B.5 Restricted contraction and visual-inspection step

key_findings.claim: The main theorem's algebra is readily repairable, but its formal presentation contains direction and symbol errors that matter for a paper selling exact characterization.
key_findings.evidence: The proof reverses the inclusion relation between match sets when one conjunction contains another, mixes S and J, writes an undefined delta_S in the key decomposition, restricts the match-set definition to test z although the theorem says any input, and ends by saying it proves a proposition. Equation 9 nevertheless gives the correct Mobius identity, so these defects do not overturn the central result; they do mean the printed proof should be corrected before mechanized or pedagogical reuse.

key_findings.claim: The final paper's statement that the repository contains the code required to reproduce all experiments is false for the reviewed v3 revision.
key_findings.evidence: The official repository ends at commit 20de90e7f1a8e7e1fd727128916020450a58ea6b dated 2024-08-27, before arXiv v2 and v3. It has no DSprites/1,800-model pipeline, no random-Gaussian representation experiments, no variance-ratio analysis, and no source for Figures 6-8 added to v3. It also omits all collated numeric outputs consumed by the RMarkdown scripts and gives no experiment config for the documented C17 deep-equivalence folder. The repository can support much of the original controlled study, but not all experiments in the final paper.

key_findings.claim: The released artifact is useful but not a push-button or independently checked reproduction package.
key_findings.evidence: The 98-file repository contains 34 Python files, 29 experiment YAMLs, 11 RMarkdown analyses, and 15 prebuilt PDFs; all Python parses under the specified Python 3.11 and all 36 YAML/YML files parse. However, 28 experiment configs default to a site-specific Slurm launcher, there are no tests, license, tags, releases, raw/collated results, R environment, or compute manifest. `collate.py` references nonexistent `args.folder` when no save folder is supplied, uses eval on user text, and the figure scripts require manually edited output paths. Static syntax checks cannot establish numerical reproduction, and no expensive GPU run was attempted.

key_findings.claim: The source artifact preserves every paper visual and can reproduce the 40-page layout, but its bibliography is not cleanly rebuildable from source.
key_findings.evidence: All 19 numbered figure environments and 20 included graphics resolve; direct PDF compilation using the supplied generated BBL produces 40 pages. A standard Latexmk/BibTeX rebuild stops on six duplicated bibliography keys and leaves citations/references unresolved, while ten additional image assets are unused revisions. This is a source-hygiene and provenance problem rather than evidence against the scientific results.

key_findings.claim: The strongest novelty is the exact overlap-kernel decomposition plus the named salience/failure-mode analysis, not a general theory of compositional generalization for deep learning.
key_findings.evidence: Pre-v1 work already studied unseen-domain minimum-degree bias, compositional data-generating processes, object-centric identifiability, additive decoders, modular identification, and conjunctivity in transitive inference. A concurrent preprint even used the title 'A General Theory for Compositional Generalization.' This paper distinctively unifies arbitrary finite categorical targets and supports through one overlap-kernel theorem, then derives memorable addition/context failure modes. Later work on forced rendering, data diversity, shared circuits, sparse coding, modular interfaces, and causal composition supplies mechanisms beyond its fixed readout.

method.core_idea: Reduce compositional generalization to the geometry of an overlap-symmetric kernel and the support pattern of observed categorical component combinations, then use Mobius inversion and minimum-norm interpolation to identify which conjunction-specific terms can influence each unseen input.
method.mechanism: Inputs z have C finite discrete components. A fixed representation or infinite-width random transform induces a kernel whose value depends only on the matched component positions. The kernel is decomposed into indicator kernels for every subset J of components. Training a zero-initialized linear readout/minimum-norm kernel predictor changes only features attached to conjunction values present in training, yielding conjunction-wise additive test predictions. A normalized Mobius transform of overlap similarities is called representational salience and is used to predict how minimum norm divides weight among component and conjunction terms. Hand-specified kernels, rich/lazy ReLU networks, MNIST ConvNets, CIFAR-10 ResNets/ViTs, Gaussian random representations, and pretrained DSprites VAE embeddings test the resulting task and geometry predictions.
assumptions: The input has a fixed finite number of discrete categorical components with known component identity.
Train and test differ by held-out Cartesian combinations, and the relevant support set is known exactly.
The fixed kernel depends only on the number or identity of exactly matching component positions, not on matched values or within-factor distance.
The learned function lies in the span of training representations, as for a zero-initialized linear readout or representer-form minimum-norm kernel method.
Kernel regression matrices are invertible where K inverse is used, or an unstated pseudoinverse/regularized limit supplies the intended solution.
Scalar-output regression or binary decision margins adequately represent the compositional task; multidimensional outputs are treated coordinate-wise.
The salience normalization denominator is nonzero and the Mobius coefficients have an interpretation appropriate for the plotted kernels.
Minimum L2-norm is the relevant implicit bias; optimizer, initialization, regularization, early stopping, and loss do not select a materially different interpolant.
For Proposition 5.1, component values and the observed subset are centered and training support consists of complete selected rows and columns.
For the Gaussian extension, every conjunction-value vector is independent, isotropic, and zero mean, and ensemble expectation is the relevant notion of systematic behavior.
For vision experiments, category permutation, spatial separation, and averaging over image instances isolate the intended component geometry.
Qualitative alignment between feature-learning networks and kernel predictions is informative even though their NTK changes during training.
The conjunction-wise linear R-squared diagnostic is not spuriously high because the evaluation grid is small, averaged, or fit and scored on overlapping structures.
A task classified as non-additive is evaluated under the paper's exact component encoding and train/test support, rather than under any possible re-encoding.
The sparse shared-unit account for rich ReLU transitive equivalence generalizes beyond the visualized seeds and settings.

techniques.role: Constrains similarity to depend only on matched component positions.
Decomposes each overlap similarity into unique terms for all component subsets.
Expresses a learned prediction as a sum over conjunction values observed in training.
Normalizes Mobius overlap increments to summarize representational geometry.
Selects how training labels are distributed among redundant component and conjunction features.
Derives the closed-form compression factor for centered symbolic-addition splits.
Maps context-dependence success regions over first-, second-, and third-order saliences.
Uses transitive equivalence as a non-additive negative control for fixed kernels.
Propagates overlap structure through infinite-width random neural kernels.
Extends conjunction additivity in expectation to independent random conjunction codes.
Fits all training-supported conjunction indicators to model predictions and reports R-squared.
Compares pre- and post-training NTK salience to test whether a deep model remained in kernel regime.
Varies initialization scale to contrast feature-learning and lazy ReLU solutions.
Builds controlled MNIST/CIFAR inputs by stacking category images in channels with variable spatial offsets.
Randomizes category-to-component roles to average away value-specific similarity structure.
Measures residual similarity variance after projecting learned embeddings onto an overlap-structured kernel.

evaluations.setting: Arbitrary finite categorical targets with a fixed compositionally structured kernel.
evaluations.metric: Exact functional characterization on every input.
evaluations.result: Theorem 4.2 yields a sum over only those component conjunction values represented in training.
evaluations.baseline: An unrestricted interpolating function whose unseen behavior is unconstrained.

evaluations.setting: Centered symbolic addition with selected complete rows and columns.
evaluations.metric: Held-out prediction slope relative to the true sum.
evaluations.result: The exact slope depends only on S(1;2) and observed-subset size p and is below one when full-conjunction salience is positive.
evaluations.baseline: A purely component-wise additive representation with slope one.

evaluations.setting: Three-component context dependence under CD-1, CD-2, and CD-3 support patterns.
evaluations.metric: Held-out classification accuracy and inferred conjunction-weight magnitudes.
evaluations.result: CD-3 fails when context/full-conjunction shortcuts dominate correct context-feature pair terms; weaker held-out splits generalize over a wider salience region.
evaluations.baseline: The correct pairwise context-feature solution and chance accuracy.

evaluations.setting: Transitive equivalence versus transitive ordering on discrete pairs.
evaluations.metric: Possibility of correct unseen-pair prediction under conjunction-wise additivity.
evaluations.result: Fixed kernels cannot systematically solve the equivalence split but can implement ordering through item-rank differences.
evaluations.baseline: An unrestricted pair memorizer and a component-wise rank representation.

evaluations.setting: Random infinite-width networks over multi-hot component inputs.
evaluations.metric: Order-specific salience across depth and nonlinearity.
evaluations.result: Numerical kernels shift mass toward higher-order conjunctions with depth; the printed infinite-depth ReLU proof is incomplete as written.
evaluations.baseline: The input multi-hot kernel with only first-order salience.

evaluations.setting: Independent Gaussian conjunction codes of dimension 100.
evaluations.metric: Conjunction-additivity R-squared, addition slope, context accuracy, and equivalence accuracy over 100 representation samples.
evaluations.result: The ensemble average is additive and follows qualitative predictions, while individual draws may be strongly non-additive.
evaluations.baseline: The exactly overlap-structured expected kernel and each individual random representation.

evaluations.setting: MNIST symbolic addition with ConvNets and variable component distance.
evaluations.metric: Intermediate/NTK S(1;2), held-out slope/MSE, and conjunction-additivity R-squared over ten runs.
evaluations.result: Greater separation generally increases component salience and improves held-out slope; training changes the NTK substantially and the exact kernel formula does not fit quantitatively.
evaluations.baseline: The fixed-kernel slope curve, in-distribution validation, and zero-distance inputs.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10 symbolic addition with ResNet and ViT models.
evaluations.metric: Held-out prediction slope across distance and training-support size over ten runs.
evaluations.result: Both architectures show noisier qualitative compression and coverage trends, with a subtle distance effect for ViTs and imperfect training fits.
evaluations.baseline: The exact Proposition 5.1 curve and in-distribution performance.

evaluations.setting: MNIST/CIFAR context dependence with ConvNet, ResNet, and ViT models.
evaluations.metric: Training, in-distribution, and compositional accuracy on CD-1 through CD-3.
evaluations.result: Models generally exceed chance on CD-1/CD-2 and fall below chance on CD-3, consistent with a context shortcut.
evaluations.baseline: Chance accuracy and the hand-specified kernel salience map.

evaluations.setting: Six disentanglement architectures comprising 1,800 pretrained DSprites models and 50 task-role samples.
evaluations.metric: Additivity, transitive-equivalence accuracy, overlap-kernel variance ratio, addition error versus salience, and context accuracy.
evaluations.result: Average outputs are often additive, but representations strongly violate overlap structure, salience does not predict addition, and context results remain near chance.
evaluations.baseline: An exact overlap-structured representation and the paper's salience predictions.

evaluations.setting: One-hidden-layer ReLU and MNIST ConvNet transitive equivalence.
evaluations.metric: Learning curves, hidden-unit weight sharing, and held-out equivalence accuracy.
evaluations.result: Rich small-initialization networks learn shared features and generalize where lazy networks fail; ConvNets improve with spatial separation.
evaluations.baseline: Lazy/kernel-regime networks and zero component separation.

evaluations.setting: Official TeX and GitHub artifacts for arXiv v3.
evaluations.metric: Source rebuild, visual resolution, static syntax/config checks, coverage of final experiments, and result-data availability.
evaluations.result: All 19 figures resolve and prebuilt-BBL compilation yields 40 pages; Python/YAML syntax passes, but bibliography regeneration fails, final v3 analyses and collated results are absent, and no tests or portable runner are supplied.
evaluations.baseline: A tagged, tested, data-complete artifact that rebuilds the final paper from raw results.

limitations: Author-stated: the exact theory is restricted to fixed kernel models and does not characterize representation learning.
Author-stated: there are no quantitative bounds connecting the theory to the studied deep networks.
Author-stated: the deep ConvNet NTK changes substantially during training, so the theory does not apply exactly.
Author-stated: extremely large models, variable-length sequences, other input/output formats, and general non-compositionally structured representations remain untested.
Author-stated: DSprites salience does not predict symbolic-addition error because the learned representations violate the structural assumption.
Author-stated: the Gaussian non-structured extension has no per-instance geometry guarantee and only constrains ensemble expectation.
Reviewer inference: exact overlap exchangeability is much stronger than ordinary disentanglement, modularity, or compositionality.
Reviewer inference: the main task family uses known finite categorical factors and complete enumerated combination grids, unlike most real observations.
Reviewer inference: the salience definition can be negative or undefined for valid kernels and lacks stated domain conditions.
Reviewer inference: invertibility, singular kernels, pseudoinverses, regularization, and nonzero initialization are not treated systematically.
Reviewer inference: scalar outputs and coordinate-wise extension do not capture structured-output dependencies or autoregressive feedback.
Reviewer inference: the deep-vision evidence uses three standard architectures, two small image datasets, synthetic channel compositions, and ten joint seeds per condition.
Reviewer inference: category permutation, image sampling, initialization, augmentation, and training share seeds, so error bars do not isolate sources of variance.
Reviewer inference: conjunction-additivity is fitted to predictions on a small enumerated grid after averaging image instances and may overstate instance-level structure.
Reviewer inference: no statistical tests, preregistered predictions, multiple-comparison controls, or held-out model families accompany the qualitative deep-network claims.
Reviewer inference: the rich-ReLU shared-unit explanation is mechanistic evidence, not a complete convergence or scaling theorem.
Formal audit: the self-contained proof of Proposition B.2 has algebraic inconsistencies, covers only s at most one half, and ends with visual inspection rather than a proof.
Formal audit: the proof of Theorem 4.2 reverses a set inclusion and contains undefined/mismatched symbols, although its core Mobius identity is repairable.
Artifact audit: the official repository predates v2/v3 and omits the Gaussian and DSprites experiments in the final manuscript.
Artifact audit: collated result tables are absent, R dependencies are unspecified, 28 configs default to Slurm, and one documented experiment has no config.
Artifact audit: there are no tests, license, release/tag, CI, hardware/runtime accounting, or exact paper-to-commit mapping.
Artifact audit: `collate.py` fails on its default save-path branch due to `args.folder` versus `args.folders` and evaluates user-provided Python text.
Source audit: compilation succeeds with the generated BBL, but fresh BibTeX generation fails on six duplicate entries.
failure_modes: A full-conjunction feature fits every observed pair cheaply and steals norm from reusable component terms, compressing predictions for unseen pairs.
A context-only feature predicts most training labels and full conjunctions memorize exceptions, reversing held-out accuracy below chance.
A benchmark leaves out only full pairs, making any fixed overlap kernel appear incapable even though a different factor encoding would solve the task.
A representation has value-specific similarity or continuous factor distance, invalidating the overlap-exchangeability theorem while still looking disentangled to a probe.
A salience denominator is zero or a Mobius coefficient is negative, making mixture-style plots or causal subpopulation language misleading.
A singular Gram matrix makes the stated K inverse undefined and different pseudoinverse or regularization conventions select different behavior.
A finite-width random representation deviates systematically for a particular deployed seed even though its ensemble expectation is additive.
A deep model changes its features during training, so pretraining NTK salience predicts only a trend and not the final slope.
A conjunction probe attains high R-squared after category-level averaging while individual images contain important non-additive behavior.
Jointly changing spatial distance modifies optimization difficulty and architecture receptive fields in addition to the intended salience.
Incomplete training fit in ResNet or ViT models is mistaken for a compositional-generalization phenomenon.
A task is labeled non-additive without declaring its encoding and support, even though a rank, log, program, or relational representation makes it additive.
A rich model finds a new shared abstraction and escapes the fixed-kernel impossibility, invalidating extrapolation from the theorem to trained networks.
A random train/validation image sampler draws with replacement, allowing duplicate composed images across the in-distribution training and validation partitions.
A final manuscript adds analyses after the artifact's last commit, while a blanket reproducibility statement remains unchanged.
A reader runs the advertised collator without `--save_folder` and hits the `args.folder` typo or cannot find the uncommitted multirun data.
A normal source rebuild regenerates the bibliography and fails even though compiling against the included BBL works.
A visually plausible contraction plot substitutes for proof and hides an uncovered parameter range.
reusable_insights: Treat train-support structure and representation geometry as separate experimental axes; either can determine compositional failure.
Expand any equality-overlap kernel in the Boolean lattice of component subsets before attributing behavior to an architecture.
Report raw overlap similarities alongside Mobius saliences and explicitly test positivity and denominator stability.
Use tasks with known additive and non-additive solutions under the same encoding as positive and negative controls.
Measure both whether a target is representable from observed conjunctions and which representable solution the optimizer selects.
For addition-like tasks, vary support size independently of numerical interpolation/extrapolation to isolate memorization leak.
For context tasks, quantify the best shortcut's training accuracy and the conjunction capacity needed to memorize its exceptions.
Audit a deep model's kernel before and after training before applying a fixed-NTK theory quantitatively.
Separate ensemble-average guarantees from per-seed guarantees and show the full distribution of deployed representations.
Fit compositional probes on held-out task instances and retain instance-level residuals rather than only category-averaged R-squared.
Randomize factor-to-observation mappings to distinguish recombination from value-specific similarity, but preserve per-instance results as well as averages.
Search explicitly for feature-learning escape mechanisms whenever a fixed-representation theory gives an impossibility result.
Declare component encoding, output encoding, support graph, initialization, loss, regularization, and solution convention in every compositional claim.
Use support hypergraphs to generate benchmark families whose required conjunction order is known and tunable.
In evolutionary RL-environment search, score whether train and validation tasks expose the conjunctions needed by the intended policy rule and penalize shortcut-supported alternatives.
Validate an RL environment with a ladder of policy classes: fixed kernels detect low-order shortcuts, feature learners test escape, and larger agents test whether the signal persists.
Track learning progress, policy diversity, exploitability, and held-out recombination jointly; a solvable reward function alone does not establish useful learning signal.
Package every final-paper analysis with a tagged commit, immutable raw outputs, a portable local config, tests for analytic formulas, and a one-command figure rebuild.
open_questions: What are necessary and sufficient positivity conditions for the paper's Mobius saliences to correspond to a real orthogonal conjunction-feature decomposition?
How should salience be regularized or replaced for approximate, value-dependent, continuous, or anisotropic component similarities?
Can conjunction-wise additivity be characterized with finite-sample error bounds when the kernel is only approximately overlap structured?
What changes under ridge regularization, early stopping, nonzero readout initialization, logistic loss, and singular Gram matrices?
Can one derive a quantitative perturbation theorem connecting changes in a trained NTK to errors in the fixed-kernel slope prediction?
Which feature-learning dynamics reliably discover the shared abstractions needed for non-additive tasks, and how do they scale with component count?
Does memorization leak persist in pretrained foundation models after controlled last-layer, full-finetuning, and in-context adaptation comparisons?
How do variable numbers of objects, sequences, graphs, and structured outputs change the relevant lattice of conjunctions?
Can support-hypergraph design minimize shortcut correlations while using far fewer than all Cartesian combinations?
When does below-chance compositional accuracy diagnose a shortcut rather than optimization failure, label imbalance, or misspecified components?
How stable are additivity and salience estimates across task-role permutations, seeds, layers, checkpoints, and observation modalities?
Can causal interventions on factors distinguish a representation that merely has overlap geometry from one that implements reusable mechanisms?
What per-instance guarantee replaces the Gaussian ensemble result for a single learned or randomly initialized representation?
How should non-additivity be defined invariantly across equivalent encodings without making every finite task trivially additive at full conjunction order?
Can a compositional benchmark preregister its minimal required conjunction order and verify it mechanically?
For synthetic RL environments, which kernel/support diagnostics predict later policy learning progress without training a full agent?
When does success by a small probe or policy scale to larger agents, and what cross-size invariants are more reliable than a single learning curve?
Can evolutionary environment search optimize for a curriculum that moves agents from low-order to higher-order conjunction rules without introducing exploitable full-state memorization?
Which environment validators can be automated and which semantics, novelty, or safety judgments still require human review?
Would a clean reproduction of every final-version experiment preserve the reported trends under independent seeds, disjoint image validation samples, and held-out architectures?

competitive_landscape.title: Generalization on the Unseen, Logic Reasoning and Degree Curriculum
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest pre-v1 fixed/random-feature theory of unseen-domain generalization and low-degree implicit bias, explicitly cited by the target.
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies Boolean/Fourier degree and degree curricula, often asymptotically; the target gives an exact finite-component overlap/conjunction decomposition and task-specific failure modes.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Generalization from First Principles
competitive_landscape.relationship: Major pre-v1 theory of compositional generalization from the support of a compositional data-generating process and architectural structure.
competitive_landscape.difference: It gives sufficient conditions for inference over generative mechanisms; the target instead characterizes the implicit behavior and failure of fixed overlap kernels on discriminative targets.

competitive_landscape.title: Provable Compositional Generalization for Object-Centric Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Pre-v1 identifiability theory proving when object-centric autoencoders generalize to novel object compositions.
competitive_landscape.difference: It learns structured encoders/decoders under consistency assumptions; the target assumes a fixed component representation and diagnoses downstream kernel limits.

competitive_landscape.title: Additive Decoders for Latent Variables Identification and Cartesian-Product Extrapolation
competitive_landscape.relationship: Pre-v1 proof that an explicitly additive decoder supports latent identification and out-of-support generation.
competitive_landscape.difference: Its additivity is an architectural constraint on a generative decoder; the target's conjunction additivity is an emergent restriction of a fixed kernel readout and can be harmful.

competitive_landscape.title: Discovering modular solutions that generalize compositionally
competitive_landscape.relationship: Pre-v1 modular-identification theory and policy experiments for compositional generalization.
competitive_landscape.difference: It learns reusable hypernetwork modules through meta-learning and identifies conditions for recovery; the target studies nonmodular fixed kernels and an escape through feature learning.

competitive_landscape.title: The Neural Race Reduction: Dynamics of Abstraction in Gated Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Prior exact learning-dynamics account of when structured networks favor shared abstractions and systematic generalization.
competitive_landscape.difference: It analyzes feature learning and modular races in gated deep linear networks; the target's main theorem freezes features and only sketches one rich-network mechanism.

competitive_landscape.title: Visual Representation Learning Does Not Generalize Strongly Within the Same Domain
competitive_landscape.relationship: Large pre-v1 empirical study showing 2,000-plus representation models fail recombination/interpolation/extrapolation despite varied supervision.
competitive_landscape.difference: It documents failures across visual mechanisms without the target's kernel decomposition; the target proposes one statistical explanation on more controlled tasks.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Generalization in Unsupervised Compositional Representation Learning: A Study on Disentanglement and Emergent Language
competitive_landscape.relationship: Pre-v1 evidence that bottleneck disentanglement metrics need not predict downstream compositional generalization.
competitive_landscape.difference: It compares learned representations and emergent-language models empirically; the target adds overlap-kernel conditions and confirms the metric mismatch on DSprites.

competitive_landscape.title: Challenging Common Assumptions in the Unsupervised Learning of Disentangled Representations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational impossibility/benchmark study supplying the 1,800 DSprites representations reused by the target.
competitive_landscape.difference: It concerns identifiability and disentanglement metrics, not which fixed readout functions appear on held-out factor combinations.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional generalization through abstract representations in human and artificial neural networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Prior neural/cognitive evidence that primitive pretraining induces abstract representations and zero-shot recombination.
competitive_landscape.difference: It engineers and measures learned abstractions in a task family; the target asks when a fixed structured representation is insufficient and exposes shortcut geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: A General Theory for Compositional Generalization
competitive_landscape.relationship: Concurrent preprint, submitted six days earlier, offering a task-agnostic no-free-lunch theorem and generalization bound for compositional problems.
competitive_landscape.difference: It is broader and abstract rather than an overlap-kernel mechanism; its existence narrows any unqualified claim to being the first general theory.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Simplicity Bias towards Compositional Mappings via Learning Dynamics
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later theory connecting compositional mappings to description length and gradient-descent simplicity bias.
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies why feature-learning models may select compositional bijections; the target explains when minimum norm instead selects leaky conjunction mixtures.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Generalization via Forced Rendering of Disentangled Latents
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct later competitor showing that factorized inputs can be re-entangled and memorized through downstream learned kernels.
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies generative OOD composition and remedies failure through forced full-space factor rendering, regularization, or curated data; the target analyzes a fixed discriminative readout and does not prescribe such an architecture.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Risk Minimization
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later discriminative method and theory for attribute combinations absent in training.
competitive_landscape.difference: It trains additive energy classifiers and adjusts risk to extrapolate over special affine hulls, offering an intervention beyond the target's diagnosis of ordinary minimum norm.

competitive_landscape.title: Does Data Scaling Lead to Visual Compositional Generalization?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later large visual study and theory isolating combinatorial diversity from raw sample count.
competitive_landscape.difference: It finds coverage can force linearly factored representations and tests pretrained DINO/CLIP; the target predicts support-size effects with features fixed and uses smaller trained-from-scratch models.

competitive_landscape.title: When and How Does CLIP Enable Domain and Compositional Generalization?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later controlled CLIP study linking compositional success to domain diversity and shared intermediate circuits.
competitive_landscape.difference: It directly analyzes learned shared representations in contrastive models; the target's exact account is a fixed overlap kernel and only qualitatively covers feature learners.

competitive_landscape.title: Stop Probing, Start Coding: Why Linear Probes and Sparse Autoencoders Fail at Compositional Generalization
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current 2026 theory/experiments showing that linear accessibility and amortized sparse encoders can fail under compositional shift.
competitive_landscape.difference: It attributes failure to superposition and amortization gap and recovers factors with per-sample sparse inference; the target attributes fixed-readout failure to support-limited conjunctions and minimum norm.

competitive_landscape.title: Intervening to learn and compose causally disentangled representations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current 2026 causal representation method with identifiability results and OOD compositional generation.
competitive_landscape.difference: It changes training with a context/intervention module to learn composable causal concepts in expressive generators; the target studies what a fixed representation/readout cannot do.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Interfaces for Compositional Generalization
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later agent work constructing compositional observation/action/instruction spaces and modular interfaces.
competitive_landscape.difference: It achieves unseen interface combinations through specialized encoders/decoders and a shared controller; the target provides a diagnostic fixed-kernel theory rather than an agent architecture.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving Compositional Generalization Using Iterated Learning and Simplicial Embeddings
competitive_landscape.relationship: Pre-v1 intervention using compressibility, iterated learning, and approximately discrete representations.
competitive_landscape.difference: It encourages learned compositional mappings and demonstrates gains on vision/molecules; the target diagnoses biases of a fixed readout without an iterative representation-learning remedy.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Generalization Across Distributional Shifts with Sparse Tree Operations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later unified neurosymbolic architecture for compositional generalization under shifts.
competitive_landscape.difference: It builds sparse tree operations into the computational path to execute new structures; the target characterizes statistical recombination without symbolic operators.

competitive_landscape.title: No Zero-Shot Without Exponential Data: Pretraining Concept Frequency Determines Multimodal Model Performance
competitive_landscape.relationship: Pre-v1 data-centric analysis questioning apparent zero-shot and compositional performance when component combinations are rare.
competitive_landscape.difference: It emphasizes pretraining frequency and exponential coverage in multimodal models; the target derives exact support and geometry effects in controlled kernels.

competitive_landscape.title: When Do Neural Networks Learn World Models?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later theoretical work on when low-degree bias favors learning a reusable generative/world mechanism rather than fitting observations directly.
competitive_landscape.difference: It frames compositional success through world-model learning and low-degree structure; the target freezes representation and partitions unseen predictions by observed conjunctions.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Statistical Mechanisms of Distributional Compositional Generalization
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later statistical theory proposing an invariant measure and information-theoretic generalization bound for distributional compositional generalization.
competitive_landscape.difference: It separates data insufficiency from compatibility with a composition rule and supplies a bound; the target gives exact fixed-kernel behavior but no deep-network bound.

competitive_landscape.title: Synergies between Disentanglement and Sparsity: Generalization and Identifiability in Multi-Task Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Pre-v1 theory that disentanglement benefits downstream generalization when paired with sparse task predictors.
competitive_landscape.difference: It learns representations and sparse task supports jointly across tasks; the target shows dense minimum-norm readouts can leak into conjunction memorization even on structured inputs.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning to Extrapolate: A Transductive Approach
competitive_landscape.relationship: Pre-v1 method that uses access to unlabeled test inputs to learn representations supporting extrapolation.
competitive_landscape.difference: It changes the learning problem through transductive target-support information; the target assumes no test adaptation and asks what fixed similarity plus training support implies.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper presents a general theory of compositional generalization for fixed compositionally structured kernel models, introduces conjunction-wise additivity and representational salience, identifies memorization leak and shortcut bias, and validates these insights in ConvNets, ResNets, and Vision Transformers.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Strict pre-v1 work already covered low-degree unseen generalization, conjunctivity and norm minimization in transitive inference, compositional data-generating processes, object-centric identifiability, additive decoders, modular solutions, and empirical failures of disentanglement. The target's distinctive step is the exact finite-component overlap-kernel/Mobius characterization across arbitrary targets and support patterns, plus closed-form and geometric analyses that unify addition, context dependence, equivalence, and ordering. A concurrent broad 'General Theory' preprint and later forced-rendering, CRM, data-diversity, CLIP-circuit, sparse-coding, interface, and causal-composition work limit broader priority and supply mechanisms absent here.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Novelty is strong within the narrow fixed-overlap-kernel setting and moderate overall. Conjunction-wise additivity, salience, memorization leak, and shortcut bias form a memorable reusable diagnostic language. The paper is not a general theory of feature-learning deep networks: its exact assumptions fail for the realistic embeddings it audits, its deep evidence is qualitative, one advertised proof is incomplete as printed, and later work provides constructive solutions. The most defensible contribution is an exact support-by-geometry baseline against which richer compositional learning should be tested.

reviewer_notes: Primary-source pass completed 2026-08-23. All 40/40 extracted PDF pages were read from the exact indexed revision; all 40 were rendered at 100 dpi and visually inspected across four contact sheets, covering every equation/proof page, all 19 numbered figure environments, and all 20 included graphics. The arXiv source tarball (SHA-256 ae2d2a0e9eb89016380a4f07d378fa8258ad9b201ab4d35eb881a914b75eeb81) contained 41 files including the tarball: 30 PDFs, three STY files, two TeX files, two Bib files, one BBL, one BST, and one SVG. All 20 referenced graphics resolve; direct compilation retaining the supplied BBL yields 40 pages, while normal Latexmk/BibTeX regeneration stops on six duplicate bibliography keys. The official GitHub repository was audited at commit 20de90e7f1a8e7e1fd727128916020450a58ea6b (2024-08-27): four commits, no tags/releases, 98 committed files, 34 Python files/2,499 lines, 11 RMarkdown files/2,888 lines, 35 YAML files plus environment.yml, 185 Python function definitions, and 74 classes. All Python parsed and compiled under Python 3.11; all 36 YAML/YML files parsed. No expensive training run was attempted because the pinned environment is Linux/CUDA/Slurm-oriented and raw multirun/collated results are absent. Material artifact findings are the pre-v2/v3 last commit; absent Gaussian and DSprites pipelines; absent collated data; no tests, license, CI, R environment, or compute manifest; 28 Slurm-default experiment configs; missing C17 deep-equivalence config; manual figure paths; the `args.folder` collator bug; and replacement sampling that can duplicate in-distribution image compositions across train/validation. Competitive research checked 27 official arXiv, OpenReview, PMLR, PNAS, and ICLR primary records through 2026-08-23, separating strict pre-v1 priors, concurrent work, and later competitors. Material contradictions are the qualitative-only deep-network validation, practical representations violating the core assumption, salience's unstated domain limits, the incomplete printed deep-ReLU proof, repairable theorem-proof notation errors, and the final-version all-experiments reproducibility claim.
